title: UI contributions

This page explains how a bundled plugin adds its own UI to the app. It assumes you have read
[Bundled plugin](/en/docs/build/bundled-plugin). Plugin documents describe their widgets and screens
as generative-UI JSON instead; see [Declarative plugins](/en/docs/build/declarative-plugins).

A bundled plugin adds native UI without importing any app code. Each screen and widget receives an
object called `HostUI` through its props. It holds the app's components, theme tokens, haptics,
navigation and data hooks. Because the plugin draws everything with these, its UI looks like the rest
of the app and keeps working when the app changes.

Everything a plugin adds is listed under `contributes` in `definePlugin`:

```ts
contributes: {
  screens:  { main: { title: '专注', component: FocusScreen } },
  settings: [{ screen: 'main', title: '专注', subtitle: '专注时段', icon: 'clock' }],
  widgets:  { today: { title: '今日专注', description: '…', sizes: ['sm', 'md'], component: FocusWidget } },
  commands: { focus: { description: '打开专注', aliases: ['专注'], run: (_i, { navigate }) => navigate('/p/focus/main') } },
  tabs:     [{ slot: 'schedule', screen: 'main' }],   // only for plugins that own a tab
},
```

## Screens

```ts
interface ScreenContribution {
  title: string;
  component: ComponentType<PluginScreenProps>;
  presentation?: 'push' | 'modal';   // modal → /m/<plugin>/<screen> (forms); default push → /p/<plugin>/<screen>
}
```

A screen is a React component. By default it opens as a normal page (`push`). Set
`presentation: 'modal'` for forms. The component receives `PluginScreenProps`: `host`, `services`, `kv`,
`invoke(toolId, input?)`, `params` (the query parameters of the route) and `cloud?`.

```tsx
import type { PluginScreenProps } from '@pku-harness/sdk';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function EditScreen({ host, params, invoke }: PluginScreenProps) {
  const { SheetScreen, Field } = host.components;
  const [text, setText] = useState(params.text ?? '');
  return (
    <SheetScreen title="编辑" primary="保存" onPrimary={async () => { await invoke('memory.update', { id: params.id, text }); host.dismiss(); }}>
      <Field label="内容" value={text} onChangeText={setText} multiline />
    </SheetScreen>
  );
}
```

To open a screen, call `host.navigate('/p/<plugin>/<screen>')`, or
`host.navigate('/m/<plugin>/<screen>?id=…')` for a modal. Close a modal with `host.dismiss()`. Use
`host.components.Screen` as the root of a push screen, and `SheetScreen` as the root of a modal
form.

## Settings rows

```ts
interface SettingsContribution { screen: string; title: string; subtitle?: string; icon?: string }
```

A Settings row is a shortcut to one of your screens. Each row opens the screen it names. Apart from
these rows, the plugin's page under Settings → Plugins lists its screens, widgets, tools and
permissions.

## Widgets

```ts
interface WidgetContribution {
  title: string;
  description: string;                 // for the agent: what it shows and what config does
  sizes?: ('sm' | 'md' | 'lg')[];
  defaultSize?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg';
  configSchema?: z.ZodType<Record<string, unknown>>;
  component: ComponentType<PluginWidgetProps>;  // host, services, kv, invoke, size, config, cloud?
}
```

A widget is a card on the dashboard. Keep these points in mind when you write one:

- The dashboard draws the card's frame: the title, the background, how fresh the data is, and the
  long-press menu. You draw only the content. Adapt it to `size`: `sm` is a half-width tile, `md`
  is full width, and `lg` is a large feature card.
- Load data with `host.useToolData(tool, args, { ttlMinutes })` (see
  [Dashboard](/en/docs/concepts/dashboard#refresh-owned-by-the-host)). The app decides when to
  refresh, so don't poll.
- Handle three states. While `status` is `'loading'`, show a skeleton. When there is no value, show
  the error text and let the user retry with `data.refresh()`. Also handle the signed-out state.
- The assistant or the user picks the widget's `config`, which is validated against
  `configSchema`. Describe each field with `.describe()`, and mention the fields in `description`
  ("config.names limits it to certain canteens") so the assistant knows they exist.
- Each widget is mounted inside an error boundary. If it crashes, the dashboard shows a notice in
  its place and the other widgets keep working.

## Slash commands

```ts
type CommandContribution = {
  description: string;       // one line in the / menu
  aliases?: string[];        // e.g. Chinese names: ['余额']
  argHint?: string;          // placeholder; present = the command takes input
} & (
  | { prompt: string }       // sent as the user's message; {{input}} is replaced
  | { run: (input: string, ctx: { services: HostServices; navigate: (href: string) => void; locale: AppLocale }) => Promise<string | void> | string | void }
);
```

A slash command is an entry in the `/` menu of the chat composer. Command names are lowercase
(`^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`). If two plugins use the same name, the app prefixes both with the plugin id,
as `/plugin:name`.

A command does one of two things. A `prompt` command sends text to the assistant as if the user had
typed it. A `run` command runs on the device; the string it returns appears as a notice in the chat
and never reaches the model.

```ts
commands: {
  canteen: { description: '现在去哪个食堂', aliases: ['食堂', '吃饭'], argHint: '想吃什么 / 在哪（可空）', prompt: '现在哪些食堂还开着、人少？帮我挑一个{{input}}' },
  shuttle: { description: '下一班校车（本地计算）', aliases: ['校车'], argHint: '如 燕园到新燕园', run: (input, { locale }) => quickAnswer(input, Date.now(), locale) },
},
```

## Tabs

The app has two tab slots, `dashboard` and `schedule`. Each is filled by the enabled plugin that
contributes it, which today is the `dashboard` plugin and the `schedule` plugin. The Chat and
Settings tabs belong to the app itself. Contribute a tab only if you are replacing one of those two
plugins.

## HostUI essentials

These are the members of `host` you will use most:

| Member | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `host.components` | `Screen`, `SheetScreen`, `Text`, `Button`, `IconButton`, `ListGroup`, `ListRow`, `Chip`, `Surface`, `Glass`, `Stat`, `Ring`, `Sparkline`, `Field`, `DateTimeField`, `Switch`, `Checkbox`, `Segmented`, `Stepper`, `WeekdayPicker`, `SortableList`, `EmptyState`, `Skeleton`, `FadeIn`, `Icon`, `QRCode`, `GenUI`, `PluginWidget`, `Row`, `Column`, `Pressable`, `Hourglass` |
| `host.useTheme()` | Tokens: `colors`, `spacing`, `radius`, `typography`, `glass`, `courseColor(i)`, `contentWidth` |
| `host.useToolData`, `useWidgetData`, `useBindings`, `refreshAll` | Live data with the shared cache |
| `host.useLocale()` | `'zh-Hans'` or `'en'` |
| `host.navigate`, `back`, `dismiss`, `ask(text)` | Navigation; `ask` switches to chat and sends a message |
| `host.haptics` | `tap`, `select`, `success`, `warning` (respects user settings) |
| `host.useNow(ms)`, `formatAgo(ms)` | The current time, updated every `ms`; relative time |
| `host.useSecureDisplay({ brightness })` | Block screenshots while mounted (payment codes) |
| `host.useStoreVersion()` | Re-render when jobs, to-dos, widgets or the timetable change |
| `host.clipboard?`, `host.shareLink?` | Optional; check before use |

Full signatures are in [SDK → ui](/en/docs/sdk/ui).

## Design rules

- **MUST** use `host.components` and theme tokens. No hard-coded colours, font sizes or spacing.
- **MUST** keep all user-facing text in your `strings.ts` table, picked with `host.useLocale()`.
- **MUST** use icon names from the host's icon set: `card`, `wifi`, `book`, `bell`, `clock`,
  `location`, `sparkles`, `key`, `person`, `qr`, `warning`, `check`, `calendar`, `bus`, `food`,
  `wallet`, `library`, `room`, `school`, `ticket`, `medal`, `chart`, `search`, `globe`, `lock`, … (the
  full list is `src/components/icon.tsx` in the app).
- **SHOULD** give tappable custom content an `accessibilityLabel`.
- Copy: Chinese text is short and has no exclamation marks. English text is in sentence case and uses
  curly apostrophes (’).
